target: Je le lui ai déjà dit.
english: I already told him/her it.
tip: Double pronouns: le + lui. Le comes before lui or leur.

target: Tu me passés le sel ?
english: Will you pass me the salt?
tip: 'Me' as indirect object: 'tu me passes le sel' = you pass me the salt.

target: Il y habite depuis trois ans.
english: He has lived there for three years.
tip: 'Y' replaces location: 'il y habite' = he lives there. Position: before the conjugated verb.

target: Tu pars pour combien de temps ?
english: How long are you leaving for?
tip: Pour combien de temps = for how long (planned duration).

target: Il a envoyé le rapport par courriel.
english: He sent the report by email.
tip: Par courriel = by email. Par indicates the method of communication.

target: Je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît.
english: I would like a coffee, please.
tip: "Voudrais" is the conditional of vouloir. Used for polite requests.

target: Il est passé par la porté de derrière.
english: He went through the back door.
tip: Par indicates the way or path through which one passes.

target: Elle a peur que ses enfants soient malades.
english: She's afraid her children are sick.
tip: "Avoir peur que" expresses fear and triggers the subjunctive.

target: Nous voulons que les enfants fassent leurs devoirs.
english: We want the children to do their homework.
tip: "Fassent" is the irregular subjunctive of faire: fasse, fasses, fasse, fassions, fassiez, fassent.

target: Je ne suis pas sûr que tu aies raison.
english: I'm not sure you're right.
tip: After a negation, the article switches: `j'ai un chien` → `je n'ai pas de chien`. The `un/une/des` becomes `de`. Very easy to forget for English speakers.

target: Dedans il fait chaud et confortable près du feu.
english: It's warm and comfortable inside near the fire.
tip: In imperative, pronouns follow: dis + le + nous.

target: Je veux que tu fasses attention sur la route.
english: I want you to be careful on the road.
tip: "Fasses" = tu-form subjunctive of faire. The subjunctive stem is fass-.

target: Si nous avions plus d'argent, nous achèterions une maison.
english: If we had more money, we would buy a house.
tip: Si + imparfait, conditionnel: si nous avions → nous achèterions. Never use conditional after si.

target: Il faut que nous réservions une table pour ce soir.
english: We need to book a table for tonight.
tip: For -er verbs, the nous/vous subjunctive forms match the imperfect: réservions, réserviez.

target: Pour moi, c'est la meilleure solution.
english: For me, it's the best solution.
tip: Pour moi can express an opinion: for me or in my opinion.

target: Nous en avons acheté deux kilos.
english: We bought two kilos of it.
tip: En replaces the noun after a quantity: deux kilos de pommes becomes en... deux kilos.

target: Elle nous invite à dîner samedi.
english: She's inviting us to dinner on Saturday.
tip: 'Nous' as indirect object: 'elle nous invite' = she invites us.

target: Il faut que vous compreniez la situation.
english: You need to understand the situation.
tip: Subjunctive of comprendre: comprenne, comprennes, comprenne, comprenions, compreniez, comprennent.

target: La décision a été prise par le directeur.
english: The decision was made by the director.
tip: In passive constructions, par introduces who performed the action.

target: Il est rare qu'il fasse froid en été.
english: It's rare for it to be cold in summer.
tip: "Fasse" is the subjunctive of faire. Used after impersonal expressions of judgment.

target: Je suis inquiet que tu ne manges pas assez.
english: I'm worried you're not eating enough.
tip: Negative pairs: ne … jamais (never), ne … plus (no longer), ne … rien (nothing), ne … personne (no one). Always two parts around the verb.

target: Il faut que tu sois plus patient avec les enfants.
english: You need to be more patient with the children.
tip: "Sois" is the subjunctive of être: sois, sois, soit, soyons, soyez, soient.

target: Nous partirons à moins qu'il neige.
english: We'll leave unless it snows.
tip: "À moins que" (unless) requires the subjunctive.

target: Le match a été annulé par l'arbitre.
english: The match was canceled by the referee.
tip: 'Par' in passive voice: 'annulé par l'arbitre'. The agent (person performing the action) follows 'par'.

target: Il est juste que tout le monde ait les mêmes droits.
english: It's fair that everyone has the same rights.
tip: "Ait" is the subjunctive of avoir: aie, aies, ait, ayons, ayez, aient.

target: J'en ai entendu parler.
english: I heard about it.
tip: En avoir entendu parler = to have heard about it. En replaces de + topic.

target: Je ne m'en souviens pas.
english: I don't remember it.
tip: Se souvenir de becomes s'en souvenir. The reflexive and en both go before the verb.

target: Je les leur ai donnes.
english: I gave them to them.
tip: Double pronouns: les (direct) + leur (indirect). Les goes before leur.

target: Tu y crois vraiment ?
english: Do you really believe in it?
tip: Y replaces a + thing: croire a becomes y croire.

target: Veuillez vous asseoir, s'il vous plaît.
english: Please have a seat.
tip: "Veuillez" is the formal imperative of vouloir. Used for polite requests.

target: Je saurai la réponse demain matin.
english: I'll know the answer tomorrow morning.
tip: 'Tu sauras bientôt' = You'll know soon. 'Savoir' in future often implies finding out or learning.

target: Il m'en a donné un peu.
english: He gave me a little of it.
tip: Me + en: the indirect pronoun comes before en.

target: Elle nous a envoyé une carte postale.
english: She sent us a postcard.
tip: 'Nous' as indirect object: 'elle nous a envoyé' = she sent us. Pronouns go before the verb.

target: Attends jusqu'à ce que le bus arrive.
english: Wait until the bus arrives.
tip: "Jusqu'à ce que" (until) triggers the subjunctive.

target: Ouvre la fenêtre, il fait chaud ici.
english: Open the window, it's hot in here.
tip: In negative imperative, pronouns go before: 'ne le fais pas' (don't do it). Regular pronoun order.

target: Ils me l'ont offert pour mon anniversaire.
english: They gave it to me for my birthday.
tip: In passé composé, direct object pronouns cause past participle agreement.

target: Demain, j'irai au marché acheter des fruits.
english: Tomorrow, I'll go to the market to buy fruit.
tip: 'J'irai' (I will go) uses the irregular stem 'ir-'. 'Aller' is one of the most common future-tense verbs in daily conversation.

target: Nous souhaitons que tout le monde soit heureux.
english: We hope everyone is happy.
tip: "Soit" is the subjunctive of être. Common after wishes and desires.

target: Elle est triste que vous partiez si tôt.
english: She's sad that you're leaving so early.
tip: Expressions of emotion (triste, content, surpris) + que trigger the subjunctive.

target: Il est impossible que tu finisses tout seul.
english: It's impossible for you to finish alone.
tip: "Il est impossible que" triggers the subjunctive.

target: Va chercher ton frère, le dîner est prêt.
english: Go get your brother, dinner is ready.
tip: "Va" is the tu-form imperative of aller. But: "Vas-y" adds an -s before -y.

target: Je le vois tous les jours au bureau.
english: I see him every day at the office.
tip: Le is a direct object pronoun replacing a masculine singular noun. It goes before the verb.

target: Nous voulons que vous veniez à notre mariage.
english: We want you to come to our wedding.
tip: Subjunctive of venir: vienne, viennes, vienne, venions, veniez, viennent.

target: On va essayer un nouveau restaurant ce soir.
english: We're going to try a new restaurant tonight.
tip: `aller + infinitive` = the everyday future, like English 'going to': `je vais manger` = 'I'm going to eat'. Way more common in speech than the textbook future tense (`je mangerai`).

target: Il faut que je finisse ce rapport avant vendredi.
english: I need to finish this report before Friday.
tip: For -ir verbs like finir, the subjunctive uses the ils-form stem: finissent → finiss- + subjunctive endings.

target: Je ne pense pas que ce soit une bonne idée.
english: I don't think it's a good idea.
tip: Negative "penser" triggers the subjunctive. Positive "penser" takes indicative.

target: Nous voulons que la ville construise plus de pistes cyclables.
english: We want the city to build more bike lanes.
tip: Subjunctive of construire: construise. Stem from ils-form: construisent → construis-.

target: Nous la lui avons offerte.
english: We gave it (f.) to him/her.
tip: La (fem. direct) + lui. Participle agrees with la (feminine): offerte.

target: Je lui ai prêté ma voiture.
english: I lent him/her my car.
tip: Passé composé: auxiliary 'avoir' + past participle. Most verbs use 'avoir'. The participle normally doesn't agree.

target: Il faut que tu prennes tes médicaments.
english: You need to take your medication.
tip: 'Il faut que' + subjunctive is the most common subjunctive trigger. 'Prennes' = subjunctive of prendre.

target: Il est improbable qu'il veuille nous rejoindre.
english: It's unlikely he'll want to join us.
tip: "Veuille" is the subjunctive of vouloir.

target: Il est indispensable que vous apportiez votre passeport.
english: It's essential that you bring your passport.
tip: "Il est indispensable que" = it's essential that. Followed by the subjunctive.

target: Quoi que tu dises, je ne changerai pas d'avis.
english: Whatever you say, I won't change my mind.
tip: "Quoi que" (whatever) triggers the subjunctive.

target: Je ne veux pas qu'on me dérange pendant la réunion.
english: I don't want anyone to disturb me during the meeting.
tip: Negative pairs: ne … jamais (never), ne … plus (no longer), ne … rien (nothing), ne … personne (no one). Always two parts around the verb.

target: Il est essentiel que chacun fasse sa part.
english: It's essential that everyone does their part.
tip: 'Il est essentiel que' + subjunctive. Judgments of necessity trigger the subjunctive mood.

target: L'auteur dont j'ai lu tous les livres vient de publier un nouveau roman.
english: The author whose books I've read has just published a new novel.
tip: 'Dont' with possession: 'l'homme dont le fils est médecin' = the man whose son is a doctor.

target: Regardez cette vue magnifique !
english: Look at this magnificent view!
tip: 'Regardez' – vous-form imperative of -er verbs drops the subject. Same form as vous-present indicative.

target: Je doute qu'il vienne ce soir.
english: I doubt he'll come tonight.
tip: "Douter que" expresses uncertainty and triggers the subjunctive.

target: Appelle-moi dès que tu arrives !
english: Call me as soon as you arrive!
tip: Positive imperative with pronoun: verb-moi. Appelle-moi (hyphen required).

target: Tu devrais appeler ta mère plus souvent.
english: You should call your mother more often.
tip: Hypothetical structure: `si + imparfait → conditionnel`. `Si j'avais le temps, je voyagerais` = 'If I had time, I would travel'. Same shape as English second conditional.
